questions.question: Calculate both liquidity ratios and give a two-sided interpretation of the results.
questions.expected_answer: Current ratio: current assets R22 700 (inventories 2 450 + receivables 4 950 + cash 15 300) to current liabilities R3 800 — about 6:1. Acid test: (22 700 − 2 450) = R20 250 to R3 800 — about 5,3:1, testing payment ability even if no stock sells. Both sit far above the guideline norms of roughly 2:1 and 1:1 — safe, but the mature comment runs both ways: excess liquidity means idle resources — R15 000 sleeping in the bank is not earning the mark-up or paying down the 12% loan. Too low risks the bills; too high costs opportunity.

questions.question: Calculate the solvency ratio and distinguish solvency from liquidity with a scenario for each mismatch.
questions.expected_answer: Solvency: total assets R38 900 to total liabilities R15 000 (loan 11 200 + payables 3 800) — about 2,6:1, comfortably above the 1:1 threshold below which a business is insolvent. Liquidity is the short game (current items only — this year's bills against this year's resources); solvency is the whole game (everything against everything). Mismatches: solvent but illiquid — rich in equipment yet unable to pay Friday's wages; liquid but sinking — cash on hand while total debts outgrow total assets. Solvency also underpins going concern: carrying assets at useful values presumes a future.

questions.question: Calculate return on owner's equity and give the owner risk-weighed advice.
questions.expected_answer: Average equity: (20 000 + 23 900)/2 = R21 950. Return: 7 900/21 950 × 100 ≈ 36%. Compared with a safe fixed deposit at about 8%, the business returned some four and a half times the safe rate — on the numbers, emphatically worth it. The full answer weighs risk: the deposit's rate is promised while the business's return was earned through labour and risk and may not repeat, so a business should beat the safe rate comfortably — the excess is the wage of risk. A return barely above the bank's would mean the owner works and carries risk for almost nothing extra: rethink.
